turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess the main reason I came in is just that I've been noticing I get pulled off track kind of easily? It's probably not a huge deal, but... well, like, if I get one Slack ping, or I hear a random song lyric, or even just get an idea for another project, suddenly I've totally lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. 

I hope that makes sense? I just feel a little embarrassed about it, honestly, because I really do want to do a good job and be productive. I just get a bit sidetracked sometimes, if that's an okay thing to bring up here?

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly describes getting easily pulled off track by extraneous stimuli like Slack pings or song lyrics, as well as unrelated thoughts like ideas for other projects.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed this tendency to get sidetracked throughout your life, even going back to when you were a child, or is this something that has started more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Um... I guess, if I really think about it, it's kind of always been there? I hope I'm answering this right, but... even back in elementary school, my teachers would write comments on my report cards about it. They usually framed it nicely, but they did say I had a tendency to rush through my worksheets and, um, lose track of the directions. And I guess I sometimes talked over my classmates during group work? I always felt so bad about that when they brought it up, I just got really eager to share, you know? 

And at home... my parents were really sweet and they actually used to sit right beside me while I did my homework. Not because I couldn't understand the material or anything! Just because, well, I would kind of wander off or start a totally different activity before finishing the first one if they weren't there to keep me company. 

Is... is that the kind of childhood stuff you're asking about? I hope I'm not oversharing!

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions a tendency to 'rush through my worksheets,' which indicates a failure to give close attention to details.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes wandering off and starting new activities before finishing the first one, demonstrating difficulty sustaining attention on tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports losing track of directions and failing to finish homework without parental supervision.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits to having 'talked over my classmates during group work,' which is a clear example of interrupting others.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient denies feeling like they had an internal motor keeping them moving when they were younger.

turns.doctor_question: In your day-to-day life now, do you often find yourself feeling restless or like you have a hard time waiting for your turn in conversations?
turns.patient_response:
Um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try to be polite and listen when other people are talking, but... well, if I have to sit still through a really long Zoom call for one of my classes, or if I'm just supposed to quietly study in one spot for a while, I do start to feel... kind of an uncomfortable pressure? 

It's not a big deal, really! It's just this feeling in my body like I need to get up and pace around, or at least do something with my hands. I usually just try to doodle or fiddle with a pen so I don't bother anyone. I hope that doesn't make me sound too impatient or anything? symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an uncomfortable pressure in their body and a feeling like they need to get up and pace around when required to sit still.

turns.doctor_question: When you have a large project to complete, do you find it difficult to organize your tasks or keep track of all the steps needed to finish them?
turns.patient_response:
Um... I wouldn't say I find it super difficult? I mean, I can definitely get things done! I usually try to make a list or something so I know what I'm supposed to do. 

Sometimes, I guess, if it's a really huge project with a ton of little moving parts, it can feel a tiny bit overwhelming at first? But I think that's pretty normal for college, right? Everyone gets a little stressed out by big assignments. I usually figure it out eventually, even if I have to kind of... jump around between different parts of the project instead of doing it perfectly in order. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm disorganized! I really do try my best to keep everything straight. Did I answer that okay?

turns.doctor_question: Looking back over the past six months, how often would you say you have felt the need to get up and leave your seat or move around during situations where you are expected to remain still?
turns.patient_response:

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they do not get up and leave their seat during classes unless they are on a break.

turns.doctor_question: In your daily life, do you often lose things that you need to get your work or other tasks done, like your keys, phone, or important documents?
turns.patient_response:
Um... lose things? No, I don't think I do that very often. I mean, I'm pretty careful with my stuff, especially important things like my phone or my keys.

But I always find it right away! It's never anything major, and I always make sure I have what I need before I head to class. 

I think everyone misplaces little things sometimes, right? Especially when you're studying hard and have a lot on your mind. I really try to be responsible and keep track of my belongings. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound careless!

turns.doctor_question: In your daily interactions or class participation, do you frequently blurt out answers before a question has been completed or find it difficult to wait for your turn in group settings?
turns.patient_response:

symptom_reasoning.S017: The patient admits to getting antsy and feeling eager to jump in before it is officially their turn when waiting in lines or during check-ins.

turns.doctor_question: When you are working on your assignments or tasks, do you often find that you make careless mistakes because you didn't notice a small detail or didn't pay close enough attention?
turns.patient_response:
Um... careless mistakes? I try really, really hard not to make them. I always want my work to look professional and show that I care about the class.

It's never because I don't care, though! I just get really focused on the big picture of the design or the data, and sometimes those tiny details just slip by me. turns.patient_response:
Um... forgetting routine tasks? I really pride myself on being dependable, so I try my absolute best to stay on top of my schedule. I don't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them. 

I guess... well, occasionally, I might slip up with a few basic things? Like, if I'm doing a little freelance design work on the side, I might accidentally forget to return a client call right away, or send a quick follow-up email. Or, um, maybe I'll head out to an art meetup and realize I forgot to bring my sketchbook with me. 

But I really try to prevent that! I'm actually very proactive—I set multiple reminders on my phone for absolutely everything because I want to be super organized. I always tell myself I'll do it the very second I finish what I'm doing, but then... I kind of forget again. 

I always feel so awful when that happens, because I really don't want to come across as flaky or lazy. I think it's pretty normal to accidentally dismiss a notification when you're super busy, don't you think? I really hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible... I promise I try my hardest to keep track of it all. Does that make sense?
